name: Johan Cruyff
scopeNote: Cruyff as manager only. Ajax 1985-88 (officially technical director with three assistants because he lacked diplomas; NOS: 'In 1985 begint Cruijff officieel als trainer'; KNVB gave him the diploma in January 1986 per FourFourTwo) and Barcelona 1988-96 (announced 4 May 1988 per FourFourTwo; sacked May 1996, exact day 18 May not found in a read page). Ajax start (June 1985) and end (January 1988, resigned per NOS) are month-only. Style term used by sources: 3-4-3 'diamond'/'rombo' adapted from the Michels 4-3-3, positional play, rondos; false nine. Popular label 'tiki-taka' not used by period sources. Catalonia national team (2009-2013, years only, exact dates not researched) excluded: friendlies only, no competitive matches, under the 15-match threshold, no tactical coverage found. Netherlands/other roles not covered. Marking scheme (man vs zonal) not documented by any readable source.
openQuestions: Man-marking vs zonal: no read source describes the scheme. A UEFA 1992 page (not accessible) reportedly says full-backs Ferrer and Juan Carlos were picked for man-marking skills; a search-result book excerpt says Cruyff once had Guardiola man-mark Real Madrid's striker in 1991 (search summary only, unverified).
Exact Ajax start day (June 1985) and end day (January 1988) not found; Barcelona sacking date 18 May 1996 from memory, not verified in a read page.
FourFourTwo says league titles 1991-94; FC Barcelona's own page says 1990-94 in one sentence and 1991-94 in another (the latter matches other sources).
Most quotes are reported without primary date; primary Cruyff books/interviews (e.g. Marca 2011 interview, autobiography 'My Turn') not read.
Ajax Cup Winners' Cup 1987 final and Barcelona 1989 CWC / 1992 European Cup treated as major titles; Ajax 3-4-3 per VI vs 4-3-3 per other sources: formation labelling disputed.

statedView.quote: It’s a basic concept: when you dominate the ball, you move well. You have what the opposition don’t, and therefore they can’t score.
I was criticised for playing three at the back, but that’s the most idiotic thing I’ve ever heard... I much prefer to win 5-4 than 1-0.
If you have four men defending two strikers, you only have six against eight in the middle of the field: there’s no way you can win that battle. We had to put a defender further forward.
If you don’t lose the ball in the build-up, it’s very difficult to be counter-attacked.
In my teams, the goalie is the first attacker, and the striker the first defender.
If you play in possession, you don't have to defend, because there's only one ball.
Milan are nothing out of this world. They base their game on defence, we base ours on attack.
It was not that we played badly, it was that we did not play at all.
That team changed the club’s way of thinking, that is to say, concentrate on yourself and not worry about the opponent.
If I wanted you to understand, I would have explained it better.
